definition: Software or hardware that secretly records every keystroke typed on a computer or device, capturing passwords, messages, and other sensitive information without user knowledge.
metaDescription: Learn about keyloggers - malicious tools that secretly record keystrokes to steal passwords and personal information. Understand the risks and protection.
simpleExplanation: A keylogger is like having an invisible spy watching everything you type. It secretly records all your keystrokes - passwords, credit card numbers, messages - and sends this information to criminals or unwanted parties.
whyItMatters: Keyloggers pose a serious privacy and security threat because they can capture your most sensitive information including login credentials, financial data, and private communications, leading to identity theft and financial fraud.
technicalDetail: Keyloggers operate at various system levels, from kernel-level drivers to browser extensions. They can be software-based (installed through malware) or hardware-based (physical devices). Advanced keyloggers may also capture screenshots, clipboard content, and mouse clicks to bypass virtual keyboards.

examples.explanation: You download what appears to be free software, but it secretly installs a keylogger that records your online banking passwords and credit card numbers when you shop online.
Someone with physical access to your computer inserts a small device between your keyboard and computer that looks like a normal connector but records everything you type.
A keylogger is installed on computers at an internet cafe or library, capturing login credentials from anyone who uses email or social media on those machines.
